title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Clock Start, Clock Stop and Days Used
content:
## Counting clause

On a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record, counting on a clock begins on the calendar date lying the product's start offset of days beyond the date of the starting movement, and ends with the date of the stopping movement, both the opening and the closing date being included. The days a clock has used are therefore the calendar days from the start date to the stop date, less the offset, increased by one. With the offset of one day, that is simply the number of calendar days from the start date to the stop date.

No day is split: touching a date at all uses the whole of it, and non-working days such as weekends and public holidays are counted like any other.

## Which clocks run

| Clock model | Direction | Clock | Starts on | Stops on | Measured against |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| separate | import | demurrage | discharge date | full gate-out date | import demurrage free days |
| separate | import | detention | full gate-out date | empty return date | import detention free days |
| separate | export | detention | empty pickup date | full gate-in date | export detention free days |
| separate | export | demurrage | full gate-in date | loading date | export demurrage free days |
| combined | import | one merged clock | discharge date | empty return date | merged import free days |
| combined | export | one merged clock | empty pickup date | loading date | merged export free days |

## Which product governs

The rates and allowances applied to all of a record's clocks are those of the product on the record when its final clock comes to a stop, and that holds for days consumed before an upgrade as much as for later ones.

## Whose dates count

The only dates that count for free time are those the terminal and depot systems hold on record; however a customer describes a container's movements, that description cannot displace a recorded date.

## Status changes

- Once a clock that is still running has used up its free days, the record's status changes from free time running to charges accruing.
- Clock stopped follows, from either earlier status, on the day an import empty comes back or an export box is loaded, and that day is recorded as the date charges stopped accruing.

## Hypothetical count

An import container on a separate-clock product with an offset of one day is discharged on 3 May and gated out full on 9 May. Its demurrage clock counts 4 May to 9 May, six days used. If the empty comes back on 12 May, the detention clock counts 10 May to 12 May, three days used, and 12 May becomes the date charges stopped accruing.
